evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/state.rs:722 defines `pub async fn invalidate(&self, token: &str)` on TokenValidationCache, but `grep -rn '\.invalidate(' backend/servers/reality-server/src --include='*.rs' | grep -i token` returns ZERO hits outside tests — the method has no production call site anywhere in reality-server. It is unwired dead code that signals an intended-but-unfinished revocation hook.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:395-417 (sso_logout) invalidates ONLY the portal session (`state.session_service.invalidate_session(&session_token)` at :405) and clears the cookie; it never calls `state.token_cache.invalidate(...)`. The only token_cache references in sso.rs are the introspection read/write path (:774, :797, :805, :844).

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:804-855 (introspect_pm_token_inner): a PM bearer token's `active=true` verdict is cached by token (state.rs:675 set) and returned on cache hit (:805-813) for the full TTL. Default TTL is 60s (state.rs:633 `Self::new(60, 10000)`). Consequence: when a PM token is revoked server-side (or the PM user logs out) mid-session, reality-server keeps honoring it as active for up to the cache TTL — token revocation is not propagated to the portal's validation cache because no logout/revocation event is wired to invalidate(). Window is bounded (60s default) so severity is medium, not high.

Fix direction: wire sso_logout (and any PM-token-inactive path, e.g. sync_session at sso.rs:1154-1175) to call token_cache.invalidate(token) so revocation is honored immediately rather than after TTL expiry; or delete invalidate() if the TTL window is accepted as the deliberate design.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/main.rs:446, :457, :461 start the three background alert workers and bind each returned JoinHandle to a discarded `_`-prefixed local: `let _alert_worker_handle = alert_worker.start();`, `let _drainer_worker_handle = ...start();`, `let _favorite_alert_worker_handle = ...start();`. Dropping the handle detaches the task (it keeps running) but means nothing ever awaits it or observes completion.

Each worker's body is `loop { ticker.tick().await; self.run_once().await; }` (e.g. saved_search_alerts.rs:134-137). There is no catch_unwind around run_once and no supervisor to restart a dead task: a single panic inside run_once terminates that worker's loop permanently, silently halting saved-search / favorite-alert / drainer delivery for the entire process lifetime with no log beyond the default panic hook and no restart.

Lower severity (+1) because run_once bodies are defensively written (match on db.acquire, no production unwraps on the hot path), so a panic is unlikely — but the lack of supervision means any future regression that can panic becomes a silent, process-lifetime outage of a user-facing alerting feature. Fix direction: either supervise (respawn on JoinHandle completion with backoff) or at minimum log worker exit, and keep the handles for graceful-shutdown abort.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/services/favorite_alerts.rs has NO `#[cfg(test)]` module: `grep -n '#\[cfg(test)\]|#\[tokio::test\]|#\[test\]' favorite_alerts.rs` returns nothing, while its two sibling workers do have test modules — saved_search_alerts.rs:256 `#[cfg(test)]` (5 tests) and search_alert_drainer.rs:437 `#[cfg(test)]` (4 tests).

FavoriteAlertWorker::run_once is a public matching-pass method (favorite_alerts.rs:87) that drives user-facing favorite-price-change alert delivery; it is the only one of the three alert workers whose matching logic is entirely unexercised by unit tests.

Fix direction: add a `#[cfg(test)]` module mirroring saved_search_alerts.rs's pattern (pure-function / decision-point coverage of run_once's match + alert-emit branches) so the favorite-alert path has parity with its siblings.
